title: QO+R: Analysis code and data for 'A non-monotonic environmental trend in Baryonic Tully-Fisher residuals'
description: Analysis code and derived data tables for Slama (2026), 'A non-monotonic environmental trend in Baryonic Tully-Fisher residuals: empirical evidence and a two-field phenomenological interpretation', Scientific Reports (accepted). The deposit contains the BTFR fitting and residual computation, the environmental sensitivity analysis (SPARC/2MRS), the statistical resampling tests, the stratified and multivariate IllustrisTNG analyses (including the nested-model regression of Supplementary Section S4), the derived data tables required to reproduce every figure and table in the manuscript and its Supplementary Information, and the figure-generation scripts. The paper reports a statistically significant non-monotonic (U-shaped) dependence of BTFR residuals on environment in SPARC, a qualitatively similar trend in ALFALFA, and a simulation-based sign-inversion test in IllustrisTNG. The work constitutes a phenomenological consistency test of a two-field description; it is not a quantitative test of the framework and does not measure any coupling constant. Historical exploratory documents (December 2025) are preserved under legacy/ and are superseded by the published version.
references: Lelli, F., McGaugh, S.S., & Schombert, J.M. (2016). SPARC: Mass Models for 175 Disk Galaxies. AJ, 152, 157
Haynes, M.P., et al. (2018). The Arecibo Legacy Fast ALFA Survey. ApJ, 861, 49
Pillepich, A., et al. (2018). First results from the IllustrisTNG simulations. MNRAS, 475, 648
Nelson, D., et al. (2019). The IllustrisTNG simulations: public data release. Comput. Astrophys. Cosmol., 6, 2
Huchra, J.P., et al. (2012). The 2MASS Redshift Survey. ApJS, 199, 26
notes: Version 4.0 accompanies the accepted Scientific Reports paper. The interpretation offered in the paper is explicitly phenomenological; connections to fundamental theory are interpretive context only and are neither derived nor tested in this work.
